title: From evidence to a reviewed manuscript
speech: Welcome to Paper Workbench. This tour follows a small research project from evidence to a reviewed manuscript.
You will see the real interface, with invented data and simulated AI. No live model or real research is used in this demonstration.

title: 1. Start with traceable sources
speech: Start in a workspace and create a project for your research question. Our synthetic pilot project is already prepared.
In Sources, register the material you actually have, or ingest a supported local file. Record its access level and acquisition details.
Open the source to inspect captured excerpts and their locators. Here, an invented excerpt reports twelve percent improvement across ten runs.
A source title or abstract is not a substitute for evidence you have actually examined.

title: 2. Connect claims to evidence
speech: In Claims, write the specific assertion you want to use and link the supporting excerpt or research object.
The support state stays visible. Opening this claim reveals the evidence link and the source excerpt behind it.
Keep observations, assumptions, and unsupported statements distinct. Accepting an AI wording change never verifies a source or upgrades a claim's support.

title: 3. Give each section a purpose
speech: In Manuscripts, create your manuscript and add sections with a heading, purpose, word budget, and linked claims.
Our Discussion section interprets the pilot and preserves its limitations. Choose Discuss section to open or resume its conversation.
The current section appears beside the conversation, so you can work on the prose while retaining its research context.

title: 4. Save the brief and inspect context
speech: Use Research brief to record your question, intended contribution, audience, decisions, and open issues. Save it before continuing.
Here we explicitly preserve the ten-run limitation and prohibit invented citations.
Open Context for the next reply to inspect the manuscript outline, selected section, linked claims, and available evidence.
Each reply uses current context, your saved brief, and the latest twelve messages. The brief is your continuity tool for longer work.

title: 5. Have a focused back-and-forth
speech: Use conversation modes to frame the task: explore possibilities, explain a passage, challenge assumptions, compare approaches, plan work, or act.
A useful prompt is: What would a skeptical reviewer challenge? Separate supported observations from assumptions.
Follow up with more precise constraints, and use Branch on a turn to explore another direction.
This response is visibly simulated. Live conversational writing quality has not yet been verified for this deployment.

title: 6. Request an edit, then inspect it
speech: With a live provider configured, you would ask naturally for a revision, such as: Shorten this section while preserving every limitation.
For this offline demonstration, the special revise command supplies complete replacement text and creates a deterministic proposal.
The Before and Proposed text panels make the change reviewable. The manuscript remains unchanged while approval is pending.
Read both versions. Reject any edit that adds a claim the evidence cannot support.

title: 7. Make the proposal your own
speech: You can edit a proposal before accepting it. Open Revise this proposal and write the replacement text you actually want.
Notice that approval is disabled while your revision is unsaved. Save revised proposal creates a new reviewable proposal.
The original remains in the history. Here, our revision explicitly says the small sample limits generalizability and calls for independent replication.

title: 8. Apply only what you reviewed
speech: Choose Apply shown edit after reviewing the final wording. The section now contains the exact revision we approved.
Approval changes this section's prose. It does not change the research evidence or claim support states.
If the section or included evidence changes before approval, the proposal becomes stale. Request a fresh proposal instead of overwriting newer work.

title: 9. Undo through another review
speech: Propose undo creates another pending edit. It does not immediately restore the old text.
Review that proposal and apply it to restore the original paragraph, as shown here.
Undo is guarded too: it is refused if the section has changed since the accepted edit. The conversation retains the action history and provenance.

title: 10. Check the manuscript before export
speech: Run audit to inspect issues such as verification debt, source status, claim coverage, and unsupported numbers.
Treat the findings as work to resolve. A clean-looking paragraph does not establish sound evidence.
Skeptical review is a separate AI-assisted check. In this offline configuration its output is simulated, so it cannot replace a real methodological review.

title: 11. Export a reviewable draft
speech: Choose your export formats. This demonstration writes Markdown, HTML, Word, and bibliography files into the disposable demo folder.
The interface also offers LaTeX, PDF, and JATS. Exports include a provenance manifest and the audit findings at export time.
Inspect your exported manuscript before sharing it. Exporting a file does not submit a paper or establish that it is publication-ready.

title: 12. Expand the workflow as needed
speech: Beyond writing, Literature supports discovery and screening. Review imports carefully: discovering a paper does not automatically create evidence.
Compute provides reviewed execution plans and recorded outputs. Figures tracks source data and reviewed captions.
Manuscripts also offers reporting checklists and authorship contribution records. Submissions tracks review rounds and publication packages.
These screens are an orientation to the broader tools; their full workflows are not exercised in this short tour.

title: Your next writing session
speech: For your first writing session, choose one question and one section. Link the evidence, save a brief, discuss the passage, and review each edit.
Natural-language chat is built into the application. A dedicated command-line or M C P assistant is still future work; HTTP endpoints are available to API clients.
Use the isolated demo to practice now. Staging still uses fake providers, has closed registration, and is not approved for real research. Live-provider setup and writing-quality checks come next.
